headline: Lando Norris controlled the race from pole position to victory at Interlagos, while Max Verstappen carved through the field from 21st on the grid to finish second.
whatHappened: Lando Norris managed the pace from pole position, building a comfortable margin over a chasing pack led initially by Andrea Kimi Antonelli. Max Verstappen executed a rapid recovery drive from 21st, using aggressive early overtakes into the Senna S and extending his opening stint to leapfrog the midfield. Isack Hadjar managed his tyre degradation effectively to claim third place for Red Bull, while Antonelli struggled with rear tyre wear and fell back to fifth. Norris sealed the win by over 14 seconds, managing his late-race pace to secure the victory.
keyBattle: The decisive tactical phase occurred during the first pit-stop window, when Red Bull kept Verstappen out long to clear midfield traffic while Mercedes brought Antonelli in early to cover George Russell. This phase allowed Verstappen to rejoin on fresher tyres than the Mercedes pair, quickly passing Antonelli and Hadjar to take second.
championshipImpact: Despite dropping to fifth, Antonelli maintained a commanding 111-point lead over Verstappen with two rounds remaining. Norris gained valuable points to close in on the battle for third place overall, though Antonelli remains on the verge of clinching the title.
watchThis: Observe how Verstappen sets up overtakes at Turn 1 by delaying his turn-in to maximize traction down the Reta Oposta. This specific line enabled him to complete passes before Turn 4 without exposing his car to a counter-attack under DRS.
